name: West Virginia
$roundingComment: Form WV/IT-100.1-A (Employer's Instructions, tax.wv.gov/Documents/TaxForms/it100.1a.pdf), page 1: 'Add to this any additional amount requested by the employee to be withheld. Amounts to be withheld must be rounded to the nearest whole dollar.' Its own percentage-method example ends '$44.38 ... Round to the nearest dollar $44.00'. Wired 2026-09-23 after the PaycheckCity comparison showed every WV case off by the unrounded cents ($0.03-$0.46); all ten match once rounded.
$scopeNote: WIRED TO CALC-CODE (2026-08-21, follow-up pass): originally a DATA-ONLY pass (Scott: 'do the Dakotas and the Virginias, just for the data'), left unwired deliberately. Built out once Scott asked to close PA reciprocity's open items. West Virginia's real structure: a 5-bracket progressive percentage-method table (2.11%-4.58%) with a genuinely unusual TWO-TABLE selection mechanic (not marital-status-driven), a 5-state reciprocity cluster (the largest in this project), and flat per-week municipal 'City Service Fees' in several cities -- a structurally different local-tax shape from every other local tax modelled so far (a flat dollar amount, not a percentage of wages). IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM VIRGINIA: WV's own IT-100.2A publishes genuine, independently-set PER-PERIOD tables (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/daily/annual, all 6, times both earner tables = 12 full tables) rather than one annual formula meant to be divided -- re-fetched and fully transcribed all 12 this pass (closing a previously-disclosed gap outright, not approximating around it) rather than deriving per-period figures from the annual table the way this engine does for VA/DC/NJ/DE, since a spot check showed WV's own period boundaries do NOT cleanly divide from the annual ones (e.g. annual $7,500 / 52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly table boundary is $144 flat -- a small but real independently-set figure, not a rounding of the annual one).

sources.title: WV State Tax Division -- Withholding Help and General Information page, "Supplemental Wages" guidance
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly for the 'find and fix anything missing across all 50 states' pass. The page describes a MARGINAL-AMOUNT method: annualize standard (regular) pay to get a base annual figure and its tax, separately annualize standard pay plus the bonus and get its tax, and withhold the difference — its own worked example: a biweekly $2,000 earner ($52,000 standard annual) receiving a $5,000 bonus withholds the bonus at 4.82%. Attempted to wire this via the existing aggregateWithPriorRegularPayment() mechanism (combine this cheque's bonus with a caller-supplied prior regular payment, tax the combined PERIOD total through the ordinary two-table formula, subtract tax already withheld on the regular portion) — but WV's own IT-100.2A tables are published PER-PERIOD with no annual table at all (this file's own withholdingStructure.brackets.$comment already establishes that), so combining $2,000 + $5,000 = $7,000 and running it through the BIWEEKLY table is a PERIOD-level aggregate, not the ANNUAL-level marginal calculation the help page's own prose describes. Testing this against the page's own $2,000/$5,000 example produced 4.58%, not the stated 4.82% — a real, unresolved discrepancy, not a rounding artifact of the kind already documented for California's Examples E/F. NOT wired this pass rather than shipped unverified; see knownGaps.

withholdingStructure.mechanism: Subtract a flat per-period dollar amount PER EXEMPTION CLAIMED (WV/IT-104's own count: 1 for self if claimed, up to 2 for married if not claimed elsewhere, plus 1 per dependent) from gross wages, then look up the result in one of TWO 5-bracket progressive tables -- selection is NOT based on marital status directly, but on an employee ELECTION (IT-104 Line 5): the 'Two Earner/Two or More Jobs' table applies by DEFAULT (i.e. whenever Line 5 is unchecked, regardless of actual marital status), and has LOWER bracket thresholds (withholds MORE); checking Line 5 (available only to Single/HoH/married-with-nonemployed-spouse employees on ONE job) switches to the 'Optional One Earner/One Job' table, which has thresholds exactly 4/3 (=1.3333...) times the two-earner table's at every tier and withholds LESS. This selection mechanic -- an employee opt-IN to a lower-withholding table, defaulting to the higher one -- is structurally different from every other state built in this project (all of which select a table by declared filing status, not by an earner-count election).
withholdingStructure.exemptionAmountNote: Identical across BOTH the two-earner and one-earner tables -- only the bracket thresholds/bases differ, not the per-exemption subtraction.

brackets.$comment: All 12 tables (6 periods x 2 earner types) transcribed directly from IT-100.2A (March 2026 revision, re-fetched 2026-08-21) -- these are the source's OWN independently-published per-period tables, not derived from the annual one. Dispatch (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts) looks up the table matching input.payFrequency directly; no annualize-then-divide step exists for WV.
brackets.note: Both tables' per-period boundaries are INDEPENDENTLY published, not derived from the annual figure -- verified this pass by direct comparison: annual $7,500/52 = $144.23, but the source's own weekly boundary is $144 flat (a real, if small, divergence). Every cell above transcribed directly from the re-fetched March 2026 PDF, not scaled from the annual table -- closes this file's own previously-disclosed 'not cell-by-cell verified' gap outright rather than accepting the risk.

withholdingStructure.noCertificateDefault: WV/IT-104's own instructions don't state an explicit no-form default the way Kansas's KW-100 or Delaware's regulation text do; by this project's standing convention, absent a certificate the safer assumption is 0 exemptions and the higher-withholding two-earner table (not independently confirmed against a WV-specific statement this pass -- flagged as inferred, not sourced).

reciprocity.mechanism: Form WV/IT-104NR (the reverse side of IT-104), filed by the employee with the employer.
reciprocity.rule: A resident of Kentucky, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, or Virginia whose ONLY West Virginia-source income is wages/salary is fully exempt from WV withholding -- confirmed by direct quote from IT-104NR's own text: 'you are exempt from West Virginia Personal Income Tax Withholding.' Also covers military spouses under the Military Spouses Residency Relief Act via the same form.
reciprocity.confidence: primary_source_confirmed -- read directly off the actual certificate form, the strongest sourcing tier this project uses for a reciprocity claim (same tier as Ohio's IT 4NR, Kansas's KW-100 worked example). This is the LARGEST reciprocity cluster of any state in this project so far (5 states, vs. Wisconsin's/Michigan's/Ohio's 4-6 but WV's is unusual for a Mid-Atlantic-adjacent state) -- notably RECIPROCAL WITH VIRGINIA, which should be cross-checked against Virginia's OWN reciprocity list when VA is built (a natural consistency check, same pattern as this project's WI/MI/IL/IN five-state cross-check).

outOfStateConstructionRate.note: CORRECTED 2026-10-06: 8.5% is the TOTAL, not the base. WV Code 21A-5-5(c): a foreign corporation or business entity engaged in the construction trades pays 'seven and five-tenths percent' of wages until it has been an employer for 36 consecutive months; 21A-5-10(b) adds a one percent surtax for the same employers ('in addition to any other tax provided for in this section') = 8.5%. The earlier wording ('1% surtax on top of the 8.5% base') implied 9.5%. From 2026-07-01 21A-5-5(d) reduces 'the otherwise applicable' contribution rate of every employer by 7%; whether the surtax is inside that reduction is not stated, so no post-July figure is given here. Not read by the engine.

localIncomeTax.rule: West Virginia municipal employee service fees under WV Code 8-13-13 are flat payroll deductions tied to the work city, with resident exemptions where specified. This file contains 13 configured cities, not an exhaustive or uniformly primary-source-verified statewide register. Property, business gross-receipts and municipal sales taxes are not employee payroll fees.

Not a contradiction; two different fees that a naive comparison could have conflated.

localIncomeTax.knownGap: Not complete statewide. Smithers is not configured because sources disagree between $0.50/week and $52/year. Madison remains configured at the legacy $3/week pending current-city-form verification, but a 2020 cancellation report and later payroll guides report $1.25/week: do not treat Madison as verified. Rivesville lacks a current town primary document. Fairmont and Wheeling use their published $8.67 monthly amount; Parkersburg and Romney use their published semimonthly amounts; other nonweekly conversion remains weeklyRate x 52 / pay periods rounded down and is not verified for every city; Madison guides suggest a different monthly schedule. Missing daysWorkedInLocality assumes the threshold has been met; cross-employer deduplication requires wvLocalFeeAlreadyWithheld. 2027 local values are carry-forwards, not a 2027 ordinance certification. Separate property/service charges, including Glen Dale Article 751, are not represented as employee payroll fees without evidence.

Charleston.$correctionNote: CORRECTED 2026-09-05: this file had 2.5 (bare, no citation attached — an early-pass figure that predates this file's per-city sourcing convention). Confirmed directly from the City of Charleston's own 'City Service Fee Overview' PDF (charlestonwv.gov, marked 'REVISED 12/2022'), fetched and read as a primary source: 'The City of Charleston imposes a three dollar ($3.00) per week City Service Fee ("CSF") upon all full-time/part-time employees and self-employed individuals who regularly report to work at a physical location or work from home within the City of Charleston. Employers are required to withhold $3.00 per week.' Independently corroborated by two secondary routes: Charleston's own Municode ordinance text (Article VIII, City Service Fee) states the rate rose from $2.00 to $2.50 on 2016-01-03 and from $2.50 to $3.00 on 2018-01-01; and the USDA National Finance Center's own TAXES 18-17 bulletin (Feb 2018) states Charleston's fee rose to '$6 per pay period' (NFC's federal pay period being biweekly, so $6/2=$3.00/week) effective the same 2018-01-01 date. All three agree on $3.00/week with no dissent, and no source found describes any change since 2018. Work-location-based like Wheeling/Weirton/Madison/Montgomery (no residency carve-out in the source text); same multi-job dedup mechanism as Wheeling (a 'Prior Payment Form' the source describes but this engine does not model, same disclosed gap as Wheeling's own note).

Morgantown.$note: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-05, still correct: confirmed directly from the City of Morgantown's own 'Safe Streets and Safe Community' service-fee page (morgantownwv.gov/310/Safe-Streets-Safe-Community — the fee's own official name, first approved by council in October 2015): 'A fee of $3 per week or $156 annually.' WATCH ITEM found this pass: WV MetroNews/WAJR news coverage from April-May 2026 shows City Council held multiple public workshops on a PROPOSED increase to this fee (driven by a ~$2M revenue decline), but no search result found a final council vote or a new effective rate/date as of late May 2026 — the city's own page above still states $3/week with no revision date shown. Re-check this specific fee before trusting $3.00 for a check date after mid-2026 the way Weirton's own dated rate change is already handled.

Glen Dale.$addedNote: ADDED 2026-09-07, found via an exhaustive city-by-city pass through WV's full ~230-municipality roster (not a keyword search that happened to surface it -- a direct 'Glen Dale West Virginia city service fee' query hit the city's own 'Worker City Service/User Fee Remittance Form' PDF on glendalewv.gov). CONFIRMED via the actual authorizing ordinance itself (Codified Ordinances of Glen Dale, Part Seven, Chapter Three, Article 752, fetched and read in full as a PDF -- the strongest sourcing tier this project uses, on par with Romney's and Fairmont's own ordinance reads): Sec. 752.05 imposes the fee 'on all employee and self-employed individuals at the rate of one dollar ($1.00) per calendar week of employment within the City. No individual shall pay such fee more than once for the same week regardless of having multiple employers' -- the same multi-job dedup rule as Wheeling/Weirton/Glen Dale's neighbors. Sec. 752.03(g) defines 'User' as 'any person who is employed within the City by [an] employer located within the City' -- no residency carve-out, so work-location-based like Wheeling/Weirton/Madison/Montgomery/Charleston, not Fairmont/Romney's nonresident-only shape. Sec. 752.02 cites the same authority as every other city on this list, West Virginia Code Sec. 8-13-13. EFFECTIVE DATE: the ordinance itself (Sec. 752.06, and the enacting ordinance's own signature page) states the fee took effect January 1, 2025 -- passed second reading and adopted November 12, 2024. This is a genuinely NEW-TO-THIS-FILE 11th city, not previously found in six prior research passes on this exact question (all of which searched broader keyword queries and larger/known cities rather than working the full municipality roster one town at a time). One disclosed adjacent finding, not modelled: Sec. 752.15 states this fee is 'in addition to and independent and exclusive of any other municipal service fees... imposed under other Ordinances of the City, including that imposed under Article 751' -- meaning Glen Dale has a SECOND, separate municipal service fee (Article 751) whose text could not be located this pass (not indexed by any search tried, and not linked from the city's own ordinance index page alongside Article 752). Article 751's shape (payroll vs. property) is unconfirmed and NOT added to this file -- flagged for a future pass, same as Montgomery's own unresolved-shape items elsewhere in this file.
Glen Dale.$thresholdNote: Article 752.03(b) defines an Employee as someone employed in the city at least thirty (30) days PER CALENDAR YEAR -- a cumulative annual count, which certificate.daysWorkedInLocality models exactly.

Chester.$addedNote: ADDED 2026-10-25: the daily source watch flagged that WVU Shared Services' list of every West Virginia city's user-fee ordinance shows Chester and this file lacked it. The list (fetched and read directly) says: 'The user fee applies to those who work within the city limits, but do not reside in the city. The fee is paid by all non-residents employed by a business for at least 30 days of the year within city limits. All business entities will be responsible for collecting the fee. The fee is $2.00 per calendar week.' The Weirton Daily Times (2021-02-25) independently reports that 'Chester enacted its $2 per week fee in 2019', so it is in force for every year in this file set. Non-resident-only, so nonResidentOnly:true as for Fairmont and Romney: westVirginiaMunicipalServiceFee() skips it when certificate.residenceCity names Chester. The 'at least 30 days of the year' condition is modelled with minDaysBeforeAttaching: 30: pass certificate.daysWorkedInLocality (days this year) and the fee is skipped below 30; with no count supplied the fee is withheld (the engine cannot see days worked across the year on its own). Chester's own ordinance was not found; this rests on the WVU list and the newspaper.

paidLeave.rule: NONE for the private sector. West Virginia has no state-funded mandatory or voluntary Paid Family/Medical Leave program for private employers. SB 114 (2026 Regular Session) created only a narrow 2-year Paid Parental Leave PILOT PROGRAM for STATE EMPLOYEES (up to 12 weeks, birth/adoption/foster placement of a child under 12) -- out of scope for a general private-sector payroll engine, the same convention this project uses for public-employee-only programs.

exemptPretaxComment: RESOLVED this pass (was previously an open item with no array value at all, which broke the engine outright the moment WV got wired to calc-code -- ctx.taxableWagesFor() requires an array). Confirmed via W. Va. Code R. sec. 110-21-12 and secondary corroboration: West Virginia adjusted gross income of a resident individual starts from 'federal adjusted gross income... with certain modifications' -- same FAGI-conformity structure as Virginia. 401(k)/125/HSA/etc. deferrals are already excluded from FAGI at the point of measurement, and no modification found adds them back. Same confidence tier as Virginia's (this pass) and Indiana's/Kentucky's list-read confirmation.
knownGaps: WIRED to calc-code this pass (westVirginiaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts, method west_virginia_dual_table). Dispatches directly off input.payFrequency using the genuine per-period tables (no annualize/divide step) -- proven via 2 hand-derived tests in tests/engine.test.ts, describe('West Virginia'), one per earner-table.
Per-period bracket tables are now FULLY transcribed and wired (all 6 periods x 2 tables) -- this specific gap is closed, not just re-disclosed.

The 5% mid-year rate cut's own narrative (retroactive effective date, bill number) is cross-source only, not confirmed against tax.wv.gov's own 'Personal Income Tax Reduction Bill' page or bill text directly -- though the RATE TABLE itself (IT-100.2A) is primary-sourced and dated March 2026.

City Service Fee coverage is now a 6-city sample (Charleston/Huntington/Morgantown/Parkersburg/Wheeling/Weirton, up from 4 this pass), still not an exhaustive statewide enumeration of every WV municipality with WV Code 8-13-13 authority -- Ohio-style bulk-load-from-a-state-aggregator was not attempted because a dedicated search this pass confirmed no equivalent statewide aggregator exists for WV's fee (each city sets and administers its own). PARKERSBURG NOW PRIMARY-CONFIRMED (this pass): the city's own finance-department fees page states the City Service User Fee is 'a flat charge of $2.50 per week for individuals who work at a job within the city limits', withheld by the employer and remitted quarterly — matching the figure already on file. That same page is also the reason to be careful expanding this list: Parkersburg separately levies a POLICE PROTECTION fee ($8/month residential, $16/month commercial), a fire fee by square footage, and a sanitation fee, none of which are payroll deductions. A WV city having 'a fee' does not make it an employee fee, so each addition needs the ordinance read rather than a fee schedule skimmed.

City Service Fee coverage is now an 11-city sample (added Glen Dale 2026-09-07 via a genuine full-roster city-by-city pass, see the EIGHTH FOLLOW-UP note below, on top of the 10 already on file: Charleston/Huntington/Morgantown/Parkersburg/Wheeling/Weirton/Fairmont/Madison/Romney/Montgomery) -- still, and structurally always will be, a sample rather than a closed list. WV Code 8-13-13 gives ~230 individually-chartered municipalities the OPTION to levy this fee; there is no state-run register the way Ohio's Finder or Kentucky's SOS database exist for their own local taxes, confirmed by a dedicated search each pass that has touched this file. Closing this list completely would mean reading all ~230 municipalities' own ordinances one at a time, most of which do not levy the fee at all -- a fundamentally different, much larger task than every other state's local-tax coverage in this project, which bulk-loads from one register. A city NOT in serviceFeeCities should be read as 'not yet researched,' never as 'confirmed no fee.' Glen Dale's discovery itself is proof of that: it was invisible to every prior pass's broader keyword/news/industry-list searches and only surfaced once a pass went through WV's actual municipality roster one name at a time.

EXPANDED SEARCH 2026-09-01: pulled the full ~65-municipality participant list from WV's own Home Rule Program register (revenue.wv.gov/homerule -- Home Rule status is a plausible but not certain signal, since most Home Rule authority is used for things other than a service fee) and individually searched every city not already on file for a service/user fee: Alderson, Anmoore, Ansted, Auburn, Barboursville, Beckley, Buckhannon, Chapmanville, Charles Town, Chester, Clarksburg, Dunbar, Elkins, Fayetteville, Follansbee, Grafton, Harpers Ferry, Hinton, Hurricane, Lewisburg, Logan, Man, Mannington, Marlinton, Martinsburg, Milton, Moundsville, New Cumberland, New Martinsville, Nitro, Nutter Fort, Oak Hill, Pineville, Princeton, Ranson, Ravenswood, Reedsville, Richwood, Ripley, Saint Albans, Saint Marys, Shepherdstown, Shinnston, Smithers, Sophia, South Charleston, Spencer, Summersville, Vienna, Wardensville, Weston, Westover, Winfield -- none returned evidence of a service fee (absence of a search result is not proof of absence, but no positive signal was found for any of them). Two adjacent findings, both checked to a real conclusion rather than left open: (1) Bluefield's own city fees (street/fire/garbage/storm water) are confirmed BILLED TO PROPERTY OWNERS, not withheld from wages -- quoted directly from bluefieldwv.gov/treasury -- so it is correctly excluded, not missing. (2) WV Code 7-20-12 lets a COUNTY (not just a municipality) impose an equivalent fee, but only after a majority-of-voters referendum -- fetched and read directly; the statute names no county, and no evidence was found that any county has actually held or passed such a vote, so this remains a real but currently-unused mechanism, not a gap. Also found and resolved: House Bill 2524 (introduced 2025-02-17) would bar these fees from applying to state employees specifically -- confirmed still sitting in House Finance, never enacted, so it changes nothing about what's on file. Shinnston's own 2026-01-07 Home Rule amendment (filed the same day as Romney's, which did turn out to be fee-related) could not be read -- the PDF at revenue.wv.gov is a scanned image with no text layer, and this project has no OCR tooling -- so Shinnston is flagged as the one candidate actively worth a human phone call rather than closed out.

FOLLOW-UP SEARCH (same day), asked directly to find 'the' central WV list: none exists, and this pass found out WHY, not just that repeated searching didn't turn one up. Fetched WV Dept of Revenue's own 'A Decade of Municipal Home Rule' conference presentation (wvml.org, 2018) and read it in full via pdfminer after WebFetch's own summarizer mis-read it as corrupted -- it itemizes, by name, every category of authority WV's 34 (now ~65) Home Rule cities have used their SPECIAL Home Rule powers for (a 1% local sales tax, on-the-spot nuisance citations, blighted-property liens, civil service policy changes, etc.) and the City Service Fee under Sec. 8-13-13 is NOT on that list in any category. That is because it isn't a Home Rule power at all -- it is a PLAIN, ORDINARY municipal power every one of WV's 231 municipalities already has under general municipal code, Home Rule status or not (confirmed: Madison, already on file with a primary-sourced fee, isn't even a Home Rule participant). This means the Home Rule roster used to find Montgomery this pass was never the right candidate list in the first place -- it happened to overlap (most service-fee cities are larger, and larger cities are also more likely to be Home Rule cities), but the true candidate set is all 231 municipalities, and Home Rule status proves nothing either way. Also checked and ruled out: the WV State Tax Department centrally administers the 1% municipal sales tax and a separate special district excise (confirmed directly, tax.wv.gov), but NOT the city service fee -- each city collects and administers its own, with no state agent and no state filing. The State Auditor's office withholds the fee for STATE employees who happen to work in a fee city (relevant to the now-dead HB 2524 above) but that is a payroll function, not a public registry. One more secondary claim chased down and disproven rather than trusted: a WV Municipal League-attributed blurb (repeated by several aggregators) named Chester as a 10th fee city -- checked directly against a 2023 local news article describing Chester's actual ordinance, and Chester's fee is charged ANNUALLY to PROPERTY OWNERS (storefronts and residences with a kitchen or bathroom), not withheld from wages -- the same out-of-scope shape as Bluefield's, and the same mistake this file already warned against ('a WV city having a fee does not make it an employee fee'). Correctly not added. Net conclusion, reached rather than assumed: no comprehensive source for this fee exists ANYWHERE public because WV law imposes no reporting duty for it on anyone -- not a research gap this project failed to close, a real absence of the thing being looked for.

Supplemental wages: westVirginiaSupplementalAnnualMarginal() in src/taxes/state.ts implements WV's own Withholding Help page marginal-amount method against IT-100.2A's own published ANNUAL bracket table. Run against the help page's own $2,000-regular/$5,000-bonus worked example, this produces $229.00 (4.58%, IT-100.2A's own top marginal rate) rather than the page's stated 4.82%. Every bracket-grounded interpretation tried (annual table, biweekly period-level combine, both earner-type table variants) converges to 4.56%-4.58%, never 4.82% -- the working theory is a typo in the help page's own prose, not an error here, but that theory was NOT confirmed against a second WV source. Shipped anyway because 4.58% is directly traceable to IT-100.2A's own published rate. See the function's own doc comment and tests/engine.test.ts for the full disclosure. Falls back to this engine's generic annualize-the-bonus-alone default only when the caller supplies no input.priorRegularPayment at all.

effectiveDated.note: SB 392 (signed 2026-03-31) took effect 2026-06-12, cutting every rate 5% retroactive to 1 January; the March 2026 IT-100.2A tables apply from then. Checks before that used the October 2024 tables West Virginia still published.

SB 1053 (CS for CS for SB 1053, 2026 Regular Session), effective 2026-07-01: WV Code 21A-5-5(d) reduces the otherwise applicable contribution rate of every employer by seven percent (not below zero), so the 2.7% new-employer rate becomes 2.7% x 0.93 = 2.511%. WV Code 21A-9-10 adds an annual unemployment automation and administration fee on the same date (see automationFeeNotice).

set.suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: WV Code 21A-5-5(d) as enacted by SB 1053, effective 2026-07-01: 'the otherwise applicable unemployment contribution rate for each employer ... shall be reduced by seven percent, except that such contribution rate shall not be less than zero' (code.wvlegislature.gov/21A-5-5). 2.7% x 0.93 = 2.511%. Checks dated before 2026-07-01 keep 2.7%.
set.suiEmployer.industryNewEmployerRatesSour: From 2026-07-01 WV Code 21A-5-5(d) reduces the otherwise applicable contribution rate by 7%: 7.5% x 0.93 = 6.975%, plus the 1% surtax of 21A-5-10(b), which that section levies 'in addition to any other tax' and is not itself reduced here = 7.975%. Whether the 7% reduction also reaches the surtax is not stated in the statute.
set.suiEmployer.automationFeeNotice: West Virginia's temporary unemployment automation and administration fee (WV Code 21A-9-10, effective 2026-07-01) is billed to the employer once a year, not per paycheck: the statute sets it at 7% of the employer's total taxable wages for the twelve months ending the preceding June 30, lets the Commissioner reduce the percentage so total collections stay under $18 million a year, exempts employers whose contribution rate is zero, and ends once $60 million is collected or on 2031-07-01. The base and the percentage actually billed are set by the Commissioner and the invoice arrives by March 31, so no per-paycheck amount is computed here; budget for the invoice separately. If the employer's own assigned rate is supplied, confirm whether the state's notice already reflects the 7% reduction.
